newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-DETROIT LIONS SIGN BACKUP QB FRANK REICH.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-DETROIT LIONS SIGN BACKUP QB FRANK REICH.

text.p: The Detroit Lions Thursday signed career backup quarterback Frank Reich, the engineer of the greatest comebacks in college and National Football League history.

The 35-year-old Reich, who was waived three days ago by the New York Jets, started 10 games for the 1-15 Jets last season in place of the injured Neil O'Donnell. He completed 53 percent of his passes for 2,205 yards and 15 touchdowns, but was intercepted 16 times.

Reich began his NFL career with the Buffalo Bills in 1985 and was a member of their four Super Bowl squads as a backup to Jim Kelly. He joined the expansion Carolina Panthers in 1995 before signing with the Jets last year.
At Detroit, Reich will play behind Scott Mitchell, who signed a multi-year contract extension in January after Bobby Ross took over as head coach for the fired Wayne Fontes.

At the University of Maryland in 1984, Reich led the Terrapins from a 30-0 halftime deficit to a 42-40 victory over Jimmy Johnson-coached Miami. With the Bills in 1992, he replaced an injured Kelly in an AFC wild card playoff game and erased a 35-3 deficit against the Houston Oilers, directing Buffalo to a wild 41-38 overtime victory.
Reich has career totals of 5,186 yards, 39 touchdowns and 32 interceptions.
